citations.quote: A condition is negated by use of the logical operator 'NOT', which reverses the truth value

cases.reason: The reader's claim that both formats admit the same tails is wrong. In 2002 the tail alternative is '[NOT] simple-relational-operator', and the 2002 simple-relational-operator itself begins with IS (8.7.5.1 Format 1: IS [NOT] GREATER THAN ...). So 'a > b AND NOT IS GREATER THAN c' is a legal 2002 tail, and GR2b gives its meaning: the NOT joins the operator. SR3 confirms the form exists, because it forbids only NOT followed by NOT or IS NOT. 2023's alternatives are NOT | simple-relational-operator | extended-relational-operator. Its negated operators are 'IS NOT GREATER THAN' and the like, so 'NOT IS GREATER THAN' matches none of them. Probe r1-abbrev-not-is.cob: at 2002 'A > 1 AND NOT IS GREATER THAN 6' gives T, 'A = 5 AND NOT IS = 4' gives T and 'A > 9 OR NOT IS < 9' gives F, all correct per GR2b. At 2023 all three are refused with COBOL0902 'NOT before an IS-led simple relational operator in an abbreviated relation was removed in COBOL-2014'. pb1390_abbreviated_tail_and_or has no NOT IS tail.

citations.quote: where simple-relational-operator and extended-relational-operator are described in 8.7.5, Relational operators
Format 1 specifies simple relational operators
The word NOT shall not be followed immediately by the word NOT or the words IS NOT
If the relational operator following the word NOT is a simple relational operator, then the NOT participates as part of the simple relational operator
Format 2 specifies extended relational operators
NOT < is an abbreviation for NOT LESS THAN
NOT cannot immediately precede an extended-relational operator

cases.needs: a 2002 witness for an abbreviated tail NOT IS <simple-relational-operator> object (r1-abbrev-not-is.cob)

cases.reason: Format 1 is word-identical, but in 2002 identifier-1 may reference items under a CD. Those are the implicit CD data-names, whose description exists only in Annex A (TEXT LENGTH is an unsigned 4-digit integer, STATUS KEY is X(2), SYMBOLIC DESTINATION is X(12)), and the record entries that redefine the CD area. 2023 has neither. The row's witnesses (l1_display_format1_elements, l1_display_standard_device) display working-storage items and literals only. Probe r2-cd-condname.cob at 2002: DISPLAY of A1, TL, SK, DC and SD1 prints [000][0012][00][0001][DEST01      ], and DISPLAY CDREC prints 00010. Both are correct: CDREC redefines the output-CD area, so A1 overlays DESTINATION COUNT. At 2023 the program is refused COBOL0902. The screen-format licence part (B.3 with 3.1.5) is not disputed.
